definition: In the field of mathematical modeling, a radial basis function network is an artificial neural network that uses radial basis functions as activation functions.
details: The output of the network is a linear combination of radial basis functions of the inputs and neuron parameters. Radial basis function networks have many uses, including function approximation, time series prediction, classification, and system control. They were first formulated in a 1988 paper by Broomhead and Lowe, both researchers at the Royal Signals and Radar Establishment.

explainer.lead: A radial basis function network is a neural network that uses radial basis functions as activation functions, with output as a linear combination of them. It matters for tasks like function approximation, time series prediction, classification and system control.

tiers.eli5: It is a network of little distance detectors, each firing when an input is near its center, and their outputs are added up.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for approximation and control tasks where localized responses suit the problem. A pitfall is that performance depends heavily on choosing the centers and their parameters.
tiers.paperLevel: An artificial neural network whose output is a linear combination of radial basis functions of the inputs and neuron parameters. It was first formulated in a 1988 paper by Broomhead and Lowe.

explainer.example: For time series prediction, each hidden unit responds to inputs near its center and the weighted sum of those responses forms the forecast.
